brief: The canvas autonomously animates a cycle of cellular replication. Initially, a single, smooth membrane-enclosed shape occupies the space. Over time, this cell begins to contract dramatically, forming a narrow constriction point where the plasma membrane visibly pinches inward. Immediately before separation, this constriction point pulses with a bright, internal light. The process completes when the original cell successfully partitions into two, clearly defined daughter cells, each delineated by a visible membrane boundary. These new cells then repeat the cycle, autonomously replicating until the canvas fills with multiple, dynamically dividing cells.

statement: This sketch depicts an autonomous cycle of cellular replication where a single cell grows and contracts before splitting into two daughter cells. The visualization captures the biological process through abstract animation: cells expand smoothly until they reach a critical size, then undergo dramatic contraction forming a visible pinching point. At the moment of separation, this constriction pulses with bright light, emphasizing the membrane division. Each new cell inherits the properties of its parent and begins the cycle anew, creating a continuous, self-sustaining pattern of growth, division, and renewal across the canvas. The system is entirely self-contained, requiring no external input once initiated.
